correctness.rationale: Normalizing independent Exp(1) variables is uniform for intrinsic simplex volume; selecting the minimum at y and applying memorylessness gives m∫exp(−my)(1−exp(−(c−1)y))^{m−1}dy and hence aB(a,m). For the Euclidean distance, convexity reduces the maximum of distance to the inscribed convex set to a simplex vertex. A candidate nearest e_i has x_i≤c/(m+c−1); fixed x_i forces squared distance at least m(1−x_i)²/(m−1), and the upper coordinate bound with all remaining coordinates equal achieves equality. Thus d=√(1−1/m)·a/(1+a). Independently, the beta expression equals ∏_{j=1}^{m−1}(1+a/j)^{−1}. Taylor expansion term by term gives log V=−aH_{m−1}+a²H_{m−1}^{(2)}/2+O(a³), uniformly for 0≤a≤1/2; H_{m−1}=log m+γ+O(1/m) and H_{m−1}^{(2)}=π²/6+O(1/m). Finite scaled distance implies L_m a→s; at infinite scaled distance monotonicity with a=T/L_m gives limsup V≤e^(−T) for each T. The product gives strict monotonicity and exact endpoint limits ensuring a unique fixed-p quantile. Substituting a=O_p(1/L_m) and solving gives a=q/L_m+(π²/12)q²/L_m³+O_p(L_m^−4); expanding a/(1+a) gives (3) including its positive cubic correction. For c=t mL_m, a=1/(tL_m)+O_t(1/(mL_m²)), giving (4) after exponentiation.
residual_risks: The expansion is uniform for the stated auxiliary small-a range and fixed p or t in the two specialized formulas, not for arbitrary varying p or t. The metric normalization is the intrinsic metric of the specified regular simplex.

value.rationale: The exact Euclidean metric calibration quantitatively separates Hausdorff approximation from relative-volume approximation for a natural symmetric family, in a regime not addressed by fixed trisection. It identifies how close one can be at a prescribed nontrivial retained fraction, with an explicit third-order distance and a matching volume correction in dimension-dependent truncation. Even where the leading volume law is recognized in Hilbert variables, the ambient worst-case Euclidean displacement and its finite-size precision are useful, distinct geometric information; this is not a claim of value for rewriting the beta identity or the Gumbel parameter alone.
residual_risks: The phenomenon is an exact calibration of this symmetric family under the specified scale, not a general Euclidean Hausdorff–volume theorem for arbitrary convex bodies.
